11.	Summary of the Project: The study was conducted in 19 cities through 15 CCRAS institutes 
across the country with sample size of 30,000 (Test group: 20000 and Control group: 10000).
Participants in both the intervention and control groups were evaluated on the basis of Immune 
Status Questionnaire (ISQ) Score. It is a self assessment questionnaire comprising of seven items 
viz: common cold, diarrhea, sudden high fever, headache, muscle and joint pain, skin problems 
and coughing. The items are scored on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from 0 to 4. After 30 days of 
intervention mean ISQ score in Ayurveda intervention group at baseline was 8.50 which increased 
to 9.16 at 30th day (Mean difference = 0.66)  depicting the better immune status of the participants. 
Whereas, in control group mean ISQ score at baseline was 8.68 which after 30 days reached to 8.91 
(Mean difference = 0.23). The p value was found significant (<0.001) at 30th day analysis between 
the groups. The mean score on Physical, Psychological, Social relationships and Environment 
domains of WHO QoL BREF questionnaire at the end of the study was almost similar in both the 
intervention and control group.

This study aimed to determine the individual metabolites of Ashwagandha and YG, both individually 
and in combination. Additionally, it aims to screen individual constituents against drug molecules in 
databases, identify drug molecules similar to the metabolites, and assess metabolites in blood and/or 
tissue through in vivo experiments in mouse models. The study also involves identifying corresponding 
targets of drugs with maximum chemical and structural similarity, understanding the role of these targets 
in disease pathways using protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, and mapping the synergy among 
metabolites, their target proteins, and associated pathways through a multi-component network. To date. 
quantification of biomarkers is completed. The efficacy study for the test drug Ashwagandha and Yogaraj 
Guggulu in the osteoarthritis model of animals is completed. Serum & cartilage samples for the Proteomics 
& metabolomics analysis are completed. Data analysis and histopathology study is in progress.

also been completed, along with the antimicrobial activity screening of seven plants. Other In vitro and in

leaves, and Tinospora cordifolia stems, as well as goat and cow milk, both individually and in combination,

of a decrease in these cells at higher doses in the cyclophosphamide-induced thrombocytopenia model.

induced thrombocytopenia when used alone or in combination with plant extracts. The draft final report 
is under vetting.
